o: Let d_i = |nums1[i] − nums2[i]|; we have K = k1 + k2 total ±1 operations, and each operation applied to whichever array reduces some d_i by 1 (increasing/decreasing either side toward the other). Minimizing Σ d_i² means spending operations on the largest d_i first. Example 2 spends 2 ops to get diffs [3,4,3,3] → 43. Since K can be 10^9 but d_i ≤ 10^5, binary-search the final cap x such that lowering every d_i > x down to x costs ≤ K, then spend leftovers shaving elements at x.
k: Only absolute differences matter; the two budgets merge into one pool K = k1 + k2.
Binary search the largest achievable cap x with cost(x) = Σ max(0, d − x) ≤ K.
Leftover ops (< number of diffs ≥ x) each shave a squared term from x² to (x−1)², saving 2x − 1 each; if x = 0, unused ops must be discarded (going negative increases the square).

a.n: Approach 1: Binary Search on the Final Cap
a.i: cost(x) is non-increasing in x, so binary search the smallest x with cost(x) ≤ K. Set all diffs above x to x, then apply the remaining K − cost(x) operations to elements currently at x (each saves 2x − 1). Because cost(x) ≤ K < cost(x−1), there are fewer leftovers than elements at x, so this is well-defined.
s: Compute d_i = |nums1[i] − nums2[i]| and K = k1 + k2.
Binary search x in [0, max d] for the smallest x with Σ max(0, d − x) ≤ K.
Answer = Σ_{d<x} d² + cnt·x² − rem·(2x − 1), where cnt = #{d ≥ x} and rem = K − cost(x); skip the rem term if x = 0.
a.t: O(n log V) — binary search over value range V ≤ 10^5, each step O(n).

a.i: Differences are at most 10^5, so bucket-count them. Walk from the largest difference downward, moving as many units as operations allow from bucket v to bucket v−1 (each moved unit is one spent operation reducing one d_i by 1). This greedily flattens the largest diffs and finishes in O(maxV) after counting.
s: Count occurrences cnt[v] of each difference value.
For v from max down to 1: move m = min(cnt[v], ops) units to cnt[v−1], ops −= m; stop when ops = 0.
a.t: O(n + V) with V = 10^5 — counting plus one bucket sweep.

w: Use 64-bit accumulators everywhere — the initial sum of squares reaches ~10^15. The subtle case is x = 0 with leftover ops: pushing diffs negative raises squares, so those ops are wasted. Both approaches are safe; binary search generalizes better if values were unbounded. Follow-up: maximize (instead of minimize) the sum — spend ops to grow the largest diff instead.
